description: We hope to use AI and programming to make a difference in the local community via NASA data.
summary: MESORA is an AI-powered application that assists farmers with predicting their response to climate change and expanding infrastructure in their area, allowing them to account for changes to water availability, soil health, temperature, and other factors. Most importantly, MESORA reveals an angle that many farmers lack during the age of AI–how to account for the increasing construction of data centers in their agricultural practices. As the demand for artificial intelligence only grows, these buildings continue create place pressure on farms through their footprints and consumption of not just land, but also water. While the app does account for how to adapt crop rotation to evolving natural factors, it answers a question that many of us have been too afraid to ask: what happens when the frontier of AI starts to encroach on the farms that have been supporting us for centuries?
details: As AI continues to expand, what happens to the farmland that has supported us for generations? This question inspired us to create MESORA, an AI-powered application that helps farmers understand how climate change and growing data-center infrastructure could affect their land, water availability, and future harvests. Our team is from Waxhaw, North Carolina, where a 12-month moratorium on industrial data-center development was introduced in August 2026. Seeing these concerns emerge in our own hometown made us wonder how farmers could prepare for similar changes. MESORA uses NASA POWER environmental data, along with agricultural information from the USDA and water-resource data from the USGS, to analyze local conditions, predict irrigation needs, and recommend crop rotations. Farmers can also explore different scenarios, including changes in temperature, rainfall, and potential water demands from nearby data centers, to see how their farming strategies might need to change. We built MESORA using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with Codex assisting us in coding, debugging, and implementing features, and deployed our application through Vercel. What makes MESORA different is that it considers something often overlooked in agricultural planning: the impact that expanding AI infrastructure could have on farming communities. Rather than simply showing farmers environmental data, we wanted to give them a way to actually use that information when planning their next harvest. Ultimately, our goal is to help farmers make better decisions about their crops and water usage while ensuring that technological advancements does not come at the expense of the land that feeds us.
